correctness.rationale: Step 1 proves matching avoidance is exactly two-vertex-coverability because selected graphs inherit girth at least six and every non-bipartite selected graph would contain a matching of size three along an odd cycle. The star nerve gives NM2(H) ≃ H. Tree leaf links are cones. For each chord, the exact intersection of the two cone links is NM2(H) joined by one extra path of simplices, yielding a wedge of b(H)+1 circles; its suspension gives b(H)+1 two-spheres. Attachment to the previously two-connected wedge adds b(H)+1 three-spheres. Sum over b chords yields C(b+1,2). Independent complete finite face/link and F2 homology checks match all tested cases. The proof, not finite tests, supports integral/all-parameter quantifiers.

value.rationale: The result classifies a natural infinite family of simplicial graph-matching-avoidance complexes by one graph cycle-rank invariant, including nonbipartite and arbitrarily high-degree high-girth graphs. It turns many previously isolated finite computations into instances of a structural homotopy theorem, with a genuine inductive edge-link mechanism and an integral rather than solely numerical result.
